summary: Differential rate accounting causing mixed 429s for concurrent streaming and scheduled batch retries
description:
Issue summary: Customer observed inconsistent 429 throttles affecting live websocket streams while a scheduled backfill batch job was running with automated retries. Impact: streaming clients experienced repeated 429s and disconnects despite the tenant-level token bucket showing remaining capacity. Occurred during a nightly scheduled batch retry window and impacted 3 production services at NovaSearch.

Why this ticket: Customer needs root cause, short-term mitigation, and guidance on rate-limit config so scheduled jobs don't starve low-latency streams.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a tenant API key with mixed traffic: 20 concurrent websocket streams + scheduled batch job uploading 10k embedding requests in parallel.
2) Enable client retries with default exponential backoff on batch uploader (no jitter) and run backfill job on prod us-east at high concurrency.
3) Observe streaming sessions starting to receive 429 responses within 90s of batch job start, with disconnects for some clients.
4) Check X-RateLimit-* headers on stream responses and compare with tenant token dashboard for time window.

comments: 2026-03-10 08:22 UTC - NovaSearch Support (Liam Patel): Customer reports spikes of 429s on websocket streams starting at ~03:12 UTC during nightly backfill. They see token dashboard still showing capacity for tenant.

2026-03-10 09:05 UTC - Support (Maya Chen): Acknowledged, opened SUP-918273. Collected request ids and sample headers from customer. Asked for timeframe and examples. Asked whether backfill uses idempotent keys and retry jitter.

2026-03-10 10:30 UTC - SRE (Diego Ruiz): Noted a surge of concurrent short-lived upload requests from the scheduler. Observed quota-service logs showing separate meters for route '/v1/streams' and '/v1/embeddings' which both decrement tenant tokens but with different windowing behavior.

2026-03-11 02:48 UTC - Engineering (Priya Nair): Hypothesis: differential accounting and retry fanout allowed the batch pipeline to consume burst credits allocated for short-window routes, causing streaming to hit short-window exhaustion while tenant-level dashboard still reported remaining long-window credits. Recommending immediate mitigation: apply per-route isolation for the scheduled job or reduce batch concurrency overnight.

2026-03-12 11:10 UTC - Support (Maya Chen): Customer applied suggested change to batch concurrency and added jitter to retries. Reports dramatic reduction of stream 429s. Asked for long-term config recommendation and a fix plan from engineering.
investigation_notes: Checked quota-service metrics 0300-0400 UTC: two distinct counters observed - 'short_window_tokens' for low-latency routes (window=60s) and 'tenant_sustained_tokens' (window=3600s).
Dashboard showed tenant_sustained_tokens=5800 remaining while short_window_tokens dropped to 0 for route '/v1/streams' at 03:14 UTC.
Retry pattern analysis of batch uploader: fixed backoff with no jitter leading to synchronized retry waves every ~8s, amplifying short-window consumption.
Edge proxy logs show health-check probes were attributing small token counts to tenant during same window; probes accounted for ~2% of short-window consumption.
Correlation found between job scheduler (github actions runner) and batch process ramp-up causing ~3x expected concurrency due to misconfigured worker pool size.
resolution_notes: Short-term mitigation applied on 2026-03-11: recommended customer reduce batch concurrency from 48 -> 12 and enabled jitter on retry; customer confirmed streams stabilized.

Platform-side fix: engineering to implement safer default per-route isolation thresholds and add explicit 'burst_isolation' toggle for mixed workloads. Initial PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3291
Runbook update: added entry to Confluence 'Quota Accounting Runbook' explaining differential windows and recommended configs for mixed stream+batch tenants.
Follow-up tasks: INT-4021 to add telemetry for per-route short-window exhaustion alerts; INT-4022 to consider backoff/jitter enforcement guidance in SDK.
resolution: Workaround implemented and engineering fix under review
